scope: Implement PAR-127 / 7BE.10 local DWG HEADER date/time representability safety with generated cross-version and publication/retry controls.

behavior: A shared checked splitter rejects non-finite values and day/millisecond results that cannot be represented by signed 32-bit DWG day fields; output arguments remain unchanged on failure.
Finite values are rounded to the nearest millisecond with a one-day carry at midnight; carry is refused if it would overflow the maximum signed day.
The primary HEADER encoder computes all four date/time pairs before mutating data, handle, or string streams and before changing the HANDSEED locator.
The AC1015 and R2004+ auxiliary-header encoders reuse the same checked splitter.
No calendar-validity or positivity policy, DWG reader behavior, or semantic timestamp claim was added; negative representable day values remain accepted.
testCoverage: Generated tests cover zero, negative representable values, signed-day boundaries, nearest-millisecond midnight carry, NaN, positive/negative infinity, huge finite values, and just-outside day values.
All four HEADER variables are checked for non-mutating low-level refusal; exact millisecond-pair readback is checked for AC1015, AC1018, AC1021, AC1024, AC1027, and AC1032.
A generated public AC1027 write proves invalid input preserves a pre-existing destination and a corrected retry succeeds on the same dwgRW object.
All drawings are generated in memory; no DWG/DXF fixture was added.
